slides.title: Gross determines balancing allowances.
slides.notes: URD section 4.2: enter monthly Gross, set equal targets, establish Basic and Professional Allowance, then calculate Conveyance, Employer PF, NPS and Superannuation. Balance Special Allowance, then HRA. PF here means Employer PF. No circular formulas; unequal totals or negative residuals block output. HRA has no cap relative to Basic.
slides.text:
Appendix: Balancing rules
Gross determines balancing allowances.

URD §4.2
10

Inclusion = Exclusion = Gross/2
Special Allowance = Gross/2 − Basic − Professional Allowance
HRA (uncapped) = Gross/2 − Conveyance − PF − NPS − Superannuation
Negative balances block output.

slides.title: Employer PF follows three URD tiers.
slides.notes: Apply these rules in order. When Basic exceeds INR 25,000, Employer PF is 12% of Basic. Otherwise test 50% of the Inclusion target against INR 25,000. Use 12% of that basis when within the cap, otherwise INR 3,000. These are the client URD rules, not a separate interpretation of statutory law.

slides.title: NPS and statutory rates follow the URD.
slides.notes: NPS is optional; when opted in it uses 14% of Basic for the New Regime or 10% for the Old Regime. Opting out makes NPS zero, with HRA balancing the Exclusion group. ESI uses the supplied URD rate and confirmed wage-limit eligibility/basis. Gratuity is 4.81% of Inclusion. Keep rates and ceilings configurable and obtain the outstanding client policy details.
